question: Assume today is 2026-09-01. You know nothing published after this date. Estimate the total value of online shopping transactions in South Korea in August 2026, in Korean won (KRW), as it will be first reported in the national statistics agency's monthly Online Shopping Trends release (온라인쇼핑동향, National Data Office, formerly Statistics Korea).

target.what: Total value of online shopping transactions (거래액) in South Korea during August 2026, as reported in the National Data Office (formerly Statistics Korea) monthly Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향) release — the headline aggregate transaction value across online shopping channels (online shopping malls,
target.unit: KRW (current prices, total for the month)
target.publisher: National Data Office (국가데이터처, formerly Statistics Korea / 통계청) — Online Shopping Trends (온라인쇼핑동향)
target.caveats: Target period is completed relative to the 2026-09-01 cutoff but the August 2026 release would not yet be published (typically released ~1 month later, early October 2026), so the value is unobserved at cutoff. Working interpretation: headline total online shopping transaction value (거래액), all commo

candidates.hypothesis: The target is a continuation of a monthly series; recent published months (through ~June/July 2026) plus prior-year August values and month-over-month/YoY growth give the primary anchor. August 2026 ≈ latest published month × seasonal factor × trend growth.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total online shopping transaction value (거래액) for 2024-2026 as published before 2026-09-01, especially August 2024, August 2025, and the most recent months (May-July 2026); also the YoY growth rate trend. Minimum: last 12-24 monthly totals and the August seasonal ratio.
search_hints: Korea online shopping transaction value monthly 2025 2026

candidates.hypothesis: Online shopping is a large share of total retail sales; the agency's Retail Sales Index / monthly retail sales value provides a broader total from which online share can be applied. Target ≈ total retail sales value × online share.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly total retail sales value (소매판매액) for 2025-2026 and the online/online-shopping share of retail sales (온라인쇼핑 비중) from the same or companion releases. Minimum: recent monthly retail sales totals and the online share percentage.

candidates.hypothesis: Total online = mobile transactions + PC/other transactions; mobile share is stable and published. If total is hard to get, mobile value / mobile share reconstructs the total.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly mobile (모바일) online shopping transaction value and mobile share of total for 2025-2026. Minimum: recent mobile value and mobile share percentage.
search_hints: Korea mobile shopping transaction value share

candidates.hypothesis: Total = sum over commodity groups (food/beverage, household goods, fashion, electronics, cosmetics, travel/services, e-coupons, etc.). Summing recent group-level values with trend growth gives the total and cross-checks the headline.
candidates.data_to_find: Commodity-group-level online shopping transaction values for recent months (2025-2026) from the Online Shopping Trends release. Minimum: latest month's group breakdown and group YoY growth.
search_hints: Korea online shopping by commodity group 2025

candidates.hypothesis: August 2026 promotional events (e.g., Korea Sale Festa timing, major platform discount events, summer holiday travel bookings) and Chuseok timing shift the level vs. a naive trend. Identify measurable event effects to adjust the seasonal factor.
candidates.data_to_find: Dates and scale of major 2026 online shopping promotions (Korea Sale Festa, platform mega-sales), Chuseok 2026 date, and any reported event-driven transaction spikes in 2025 comparable months. Minimum: event calendar and any quantified uplift.

candidates.hypothesis: Published e-commerce market forecasts or agency projections for 2026 give an annual total; monthly August ≈ annual × August seasonal share. Provides an independent level check.
candidates.data_to_find: 2026 Korean e-commerce / online shopping market size forecasts (annual KRW), and any monthly seasonal share estimates. Minimum: one credible annual 2026 forecast and a monthly seasonal distribution.

candidates.hypothesis: Card/electronic payment transaction values for online merchants approximate online shopping value; target ≈ online card payment value × coverage adjustment. Cross-checks the survey-based total.
candidates.data_to_find: Monthly online/e-commerce card payment or electronic payment transaction values for 2025-2026 (Bank of Korea payment statistics, card company data). Minimum: recent monthly online payment value and the ratio to survey online shopping value.
search_hints: Korea online card payment value monthly

This would replace the Dec-2025-anchored extrapolation with a genuine 2026 trend and a true prior-year August base, sharply reducing the dominant uncertainty in the level and growth factor.
directions.data_to_find: Monthly total online shopping 거래액 for 2025-08 and 2026-01 through 2026-07 (and mobile share), from KOSIS or agency press releases.
search_hints: Statistics Korea online shopping trend 2026 monthly

directions.hypothesis: Find the historical August-to-December and August-to-September seasonal ratios of the online shopping series (e.g., Aug 2024 vs Dec 2024, Aug 2025 vs Sep 2025). This supplies the seasonal factor needed to convert the December 2025 anchor into an August 2026 level, which is currently an assumption.
directions.data_to_find: Monthly online shopping 거래액 for August in 2023, 2024, 2025 and the corresponding December/September values to compute seasonal ratios.
search_hints: online shopping transaction August 2024 Korea monthly

directions.hypothesis: Quantify the effect of the 2026 Liberation Day 3-day weekend and any August 2026 platform promotion (e.g., summer travel/leisure booking surge) on online transaction value, to adjust the seasonal factor. Without a measured effect the holiday context cannot be used numerically.
directions.data_to_find: Reports of August 2026 online/travel booking volumes or platform sales vs prior August, or historical holiday-week online sales uplift estimates.

assessment.note: All from the same September 2025 Online Shopping Trends release (single article, single underlying survey). They are internally consistent (p1 ≈ p8+p9 ≈ p12+p14; p4/p1 ≈ p7) but are NOT independent measurements — they are one vintage of one survey. Useful as level anchors and as internal-consistency checks, not as multiple confirmations.

All from one 2025 annual-summary article citing the same agency survey. p18/p15 ≈ p16 confirms the retail-share identity. p21/p22 (Dec 2025) and p23 (Dec mobile) are the most recent monthly levels available at cutoff and are the key trend anchors. Same underlying source as the September 2025 points, so cross-article agreement is not independent confirmation.
July 2025 (23.14 tn) and September 2025 (23.80 tn) bracket a plausible seasonal path; consistent with the same series.

Calendar facts about August 2026 (Liberation Day Sat 15th, substitute holiday Mon 17th, 3-day weekend). Contextual only — no quantified transaction effect is supplied, so they cannot be converted into a numeric adjustment without an assumption.
Growth deceleration 7.1% (2024) → 4.9% (2025) is the trend basis for projecting 2026 growth; consistent with Dec 2025 YoY of 6.2%.

p21.role: December 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW), the latest observed monthly level

a1.role: August-to-December seasonal ratio converting the December level to an August level

a2.role: YoY growth factor from Dec 2025 to Aug 2026 (roughly one year of trend growth)

methods.rationale: Anchors on the most recent observed monthly total (Dec 2025, p21), converts to an August seasonal level via a1, and applies roughly one year of trend growth via a2 to reach August 2026. Shared dependency: p21 and the growth trend come from the same agency survey; the seasonal and growth factors are assumptions, so the interval is dominated by a1 and a2 uncertainty. Failure mode: if 2026 growth diverges sharply from the 2024–2025 deceleration, the level is off.

p1.role: September 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW), used as a proxy for the August 2025 level

a2.role: YoY growth factor from the 2025 base to August 2026

methods.rationale: Uses the September 2025 level (p1) as a stand-in for August 2025 (adjacent month, similar level per the Jul/Sep 2025 bracket) and applies the ~one-year growth factor a2 to reach August 2026. Independent of the December anchor in m1 in terms of base month, though it shares the same survey source and the same growth assumption a2. Failure mode: September 2025 may differ from August 2025 by a few percent, and the growth factor is an assumption.

p18.role: Full-year 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW)

a1.role: August-to-December seasonal ratio applied to the average monthly level

a2.role: YoY growth factor from 2025 to August 2026

methods.rationale: Cross-check route: takes the 2025 annual total (p18), divides by 12 for an average monthly level, then applies the August seasonal factor and one year of growth. Coarser than m1/m2 because it ignores within-year seasonality beyond the single a1 factor, but provides an independent level sanity check from the annual aggregate. Shares the a1/a2 assumptions and the same survey source.

assumptions.name: August-to-December seasonal ratio of online shopping value
assumptions.rationale: December is a peak month (year-end/holiday shopping) and August is a normal-to-summer month; historically August online value runs somewhat below December. Using the 2025 monthly path (Jul 23.1tn, Sep 23.8tn, Dec 24.3tn) August is plausibly ~0.90–0.95 of December. Range spans a flat-to-slightly-higher August to allow for summer travel/services strength.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert the December 2025 level anchor to an August level; assumes the Aug/Dec seasonal shape is stable across years.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published monthly data showing August online value at or above December, or a strongly different seasonal ratio in 2024/2025.

assumptions.name: YoY growth factor for online shopping, Aug 2026 vs Aug 2025
assumptions.rationale: Annual growth decelerated from 7.1% (2024) to 4.9% (2025); Dec 2025 YoY was 6.2%. A mid-single-digit 2026 growth (~5%) is consistent with the decelerating trend, with range covering continued ~6% momentum to a slowdown to ~0%.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to a prior-year August base to project August 2026; assumes no major shock beyond trend.
assumptions.falsified_by: 2026 monthly data showing growth well outside 0–11% YoY.

assessment.note: Same source (Asiatoday, snapshot 2025-11-15) reporting the same Online Shopping Trends series: p1 is the September 2025 headline level, p2 its YoY growth, p3 the July 2025 level. They are internally consistent (Sept > July, both above 23 trillion) but share one underlying measurement, so they are not independent confirmations.

p4 (mobile 18.0552 tn) / p1 (total 23.7956 tn) = 75.9%, exactly p7's stated mobile share. This is an arithmetic identity within one release, not independent evidence, but it confirms the mobile/total decomposition is coherent and usable for reconstruction.

Two alternative partitions of the same September 2025 total: comprehensive+specialized malls (p8+p9 = 23.7956 tn) and online-only+combined malls (p12+p14 = 23.7956 tn). Both sum to p1, confirming internal consistency of the release; they are the same measurement, not independent.

Same source (womennews, 2026-02-02): p18/p15 = 41.5%? No — p16 states 28.2% online share of retail. Note p18 (272.04 tn) / p15 (654.88 tn) = 41.5%, which does NOT equal 28.2%; the 28.2% share is defined on a different retail-sales basis (retail sales index-based sales, not the nominal 소매판매액 total). Treat p16 as a share on its own definition, not as a ratio of p18 to p15.
Same release: 2025 annual total 272.04 tn (+4.9%), December 2025 24.29 tn (+6.2%), and the growth deceleration narrative (7.1% in 2024, 4.9% in 2025). Consistent internally; single source.
December 2025 total 24.2904 tn and mobile 18.7991 tn imply mobile share 77.4%, consistent with the ~76% September 2025 share (p7). Same release.

Commodity-group annual 2025 values from the same release; they are components of the 272.04 tn total (food 47.36 + food services 36.99 + travel/transport 32.46 + electronics 30.85 + clothing 22.00 + household 19.00 ≈ 188.7 tn, remainder in other groups). Useful as a cross-check on total magnitude, not independent.

Calendar facts for August 2026: Liberation Day Saturday 15 Aug with substitute holiday Monday 17 Aug, giving a 3-day weekend. Relevant to a possible August demand bump but no measured transaction effect is supplied.

Not a true conflict: September 2025 (23.80 tn) vs December 2025 (24.29 tn) differ by season and by ~3 months of trend. They establish that December is a seasonal peak and August is typically below it, motivating the August/December seasonal ratio assumption.

decisions.reason: Redundant with p4/p5: the YoY increase amount is derivable from the level and growth rate and adds no independent information.
The 0.8pp change in online share is a derived difference already implied by p16 and the prior-year share; redundant.
Holiday length is fully implied by p30/p31 (Sat 15, substitute Mon 17); redundant restatement.

p21.role: December 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW), latest observed monthly level

a1.role: August-to-December seasonal ratio converting the December level to an August level

a2.role: YoY growth factor from Dec 2025 to Aug 2026 (about one year of trend growth)

methods.rationale: Primary route: anchor on the latest observed monthly level (Dec 2025, p21), convert to an August level via the seasonal ratio a1, then apply one year of trend growth a2. Shared dependency: a1 and a2 both carry the seasonal/trend uncertainty; failure mode is a structural break in 2026 online shopping.

p1.role: September 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW), used as a proxy for the August 2025 level

a2.role: YoY growth factor from the 2025 base to August 2026

methods.rationale: Second route: use September 2025 (p1) as a proxy for the August 2025 base (September is typically slightly above August, so this is mildly conservative), then apply a2. Shares a2 with m1, so not fully independent; failure mode is a large August-vs-September seasonal gap.

p18.role: Full-year 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW)

a3.role: August-to-average-month seasonal ratio applied to the annual monthly average

a2.role: YoY growth factor from 2025 to August 2026

methods.rationale: Third route: annual 2025 total (p18) divided into a monthly average, adjusted by the August seasonal ratio a3, then grown by a2. Provides a level check independent of the December anchor; failure mode is that the annual average masks within-year seasonality and the 2025 annual total may be revised.

assumptions.name: August-to-December seasonal ratio of online shopping value
assumptions.rationale: December is the seasonal peak (year-end/holiday shopping); August is a normal-to-soft summer month. Historical Korean online-shopping monthly patterns put August roughly 5-10% below December. Range spans a flat-to-strong-December case.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert a December-anchored level to an August level for the same series definition.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published monthly data showing August 2025 at or above December 2025, or an August/December ratio outside 0.85-1.02.

assumptions.name: YoY growth factor for online shopping, Aug 2026 vs Aug 2025
assumptions.rationale: Annual growth decelerated from 7.1% (2024) to 4.9% (2025); December 2025 ran +6.2% and September 2025 +13.3% (a high base effect month). A ~5% YoY factor for mid-2026 is consistent with the decelerating trend, with a range from flat to ~11%.
assumptions.applies_when: Applied to a 2025 base (August or September 2025) to project August 2026.
assumptions.falsified_by: Published 2026 monthly YoY growth outside 0-11%, or a clear re-acceleration/contraction in online shopping.

assumptions.name: August-to-average-month seasonal ratio of online shopping value
assumptions.rationale: August is a slightly below-average month for online shopping (no major gifting holiday; Chuseok falls in autumn). Applied to the 2025 annual monthly average to place August 2026.
assumptions.applies_when: Used to convert an annual-average monthly level to an August level.
assumptions.falsified_by: Monthly data showing August consistently above the annual monthly average by more than 4%.

methods.label: m1

p21.role: December 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW), latest observed monthly level

a1.role: August-to-December seasonal ratio converting the December level to an August level

a2.role: YoY growth factor from Dec 2025 to Aug 2026 (about one year of trend growth)

methods.rationale: Primary route: anchor on the latest observed monthly level (Dec 2025, p21), convert to an August level via the seasonal ratio a1, then apply one year of trend growth a2. Shared dependency: a1 and a2 both carry the seasonal/trend uncertainty; failure mode is a structural break in 2026 online shopping.

methods.label: m3

p18.role: Full-year 2025 total online shopping transaction value (KRW)

a3.role: August-to-average-month seasonal ratio applied to the annual monthly average

a2.role: YoY growth factor from 2025 to August 2026

methods.rationale: Third route: annual 2025 total (p18) divided into a monthly average, adjusted by the August seasonal ratio a3, then grown by a2. Provides a level check independent of the December anchor; failure mode is that the annual average masks within-year seasonality and the 2025 annual total may be revised.

excluded_by_input_audit.label: m2
excluded_by_input_audit.reason: input audit: p1: September 2025 value is a different period than the August 2025 base the role requires; no adjustment input bridges the month difference.

kept.name: August-to-December seasonal ratio of online shopping value
kept.rationale: December is the seasonal peak (year-end/holiday shopping); August is a normal-to-soft summer month. Historical Korean online-shopping monthly patterns put August roughly 5-10% below December. Range spans a flat-to-strong-December case.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert a December-anchored level to an August level for the same series definition.
kept.falsified_by: Published monthly data showing August 2025 at or above December 2025, or an August/December ratio outside 0.85-1.02.

kept.name: YoY growth factor for online shopping, Aug 2026 vs Aug 2025
kept.rationale: Annual growth decelerated from 7.1% (2024) to 4.9% (2025); December 2025 ran +6.2% and September 2025 +13.3% (a high base effect month). A ~5% YoY factor for mid-2026 is consistent with the decelerating trend, with a range from flat to ~11%.
kept.applies_when: Applied to a 2025 base (August or September 2025) to project August 2026.
kept.falsified_by: Published 2026 monthly YoY growth outside 0-11%, or a clear re-acceleration/contraction in online shopping.

kept.name: August-to-average-month seasonal ratio of online shopping value
kept.rationale: August is a slightly below-average month for online shopping (no major gifting holiday; Chuseok falls in autumn). Applied to the 2025 annual monthly average to place August 2026.
kept.applies_when: Used to convert an annual-average monthly level to an August level.
kept.falsified_by: Monthly data showing August consistently above the annual monthly average by more than 4%.

published.note: not checked: backtest or scored question (as_of before today, or an official value is registered), so the target cannot have been published by as_of

Two routes were averaged: m1 anchors on the observed December 2025 level ([[p21_value]]) and applies an August-to-December seasonal ratio ([[a1_value]]) plus one year of growth ([[a2_value]]), giving [[m1_estimate]] [[unit]] at weight [[m1_weight]]. m2 divides the observed 2025 annual total ([[p18_value]]) into a monthly average, applies an August seasonal ratio ([[a3_value]]) and the same growth factor, giving [[m2_estimate]] [[unit]] at weight [[m2_weight]].

The best estimate for total online shopping transaction value (거래액) in South Korea for August 2026, as would be reported in the National Data Office's Online Shopping Trends release, is 23,399,920,038,686 KRW (80% model-based interval 15,548,354,590,014 to 35,216,347,469,241 KRW).

Two routes were averaged: m1 anchors on the observed December 2025 level (24,290,400,000,000 KRW) and applies an August-to-December seasonal ratio (0.93) plus one year of growth (1.05), giving 23,781,515,418,678 KRW at weight 50%. m2 divides the observed 2025 annual total (272,039,800,000,000 KRW) into a monthly average, applies an August seasonal ratio (0.97) and the same growth factor, giving 23,024,447,692,969 KRW at weight 50%.

Only the two anchor points are observed; the seasonal ratios and growth factor are analyst assumptions, so the interval reflects input uncertainty, not demonstrated accuracy. The main risk is a structural break in 2026 online shopping. Timelier 2026 monthly data would most improve the estimate.

Key assumptions (proposed by the analyst model, not observed; code samples each one between the bounds shown):
- a1 August-to-December seasonal ratio of online shopping value: 0.93 ratio, range 0.6584 to 1.317 (range widened by code); used by m1. Overturned by: Published monthly data showing August 2025 at or above December 2025, or an August/December ratio outside [n]-[n].
- a2 YoY growth factor for online shopping, Aug 2026 vs Aug 2025: 1.05 ratio, range 0.9423 to 1.178 (range widened by code); used by m1, m2. Overturned by: Published 2026 monthly YoY growth outside [n]-[n], or a clear re-acceleration/contraction in online shopping.
- a3 August-to-average-month seasonal ratio of online shopping value: 0.97 ratio, range 0.6841 to 1.368 (range widened by code); used by m2. Overturned by: Monthly data showing August consistently above the annual monthly average by more than [n].

by_construction: Only URLs leave the searcher (code regex); extractor, judge and final prompts never contain search result titles, snippets or the searcher's text. This holds by construction and is not measured.
residual_risks: The searcher sees post-cutoff search results and chooses which URLs are fetched, so page selection can be conditioned on the answer; only the URLs leave the searcher, and in backtests every fetched page is a snapshot dated <= as_of.
Live pages are used only when as_of is today; in backtests every page is an archived snapshot dated <= as_of.
The leak sentinel only catches registered official values in common formats, not paraphrased or derived numbers.
The model's own training data (knowledge cutoff unpublished) can include history before as_of; it cannot include the target if the target was published after the model's release.
Wayback snapshots are captured by a third party; a snapshot date <= as_of proves the content existed by then.
Assumption values are proposed by the judge model from its own knowledge, which can include the target's history before as_of; code checks their form, not where the number came from.
